quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that clearly states a cause and its effect.
quests.prompt: Claim: Street festivals help local businesses.
options: Street festivals are held every summer in many towns across the region, and most of them last a weekend.
Because thousands of visitors walk down Harbour Road during the festival, its cafés sell out by noon.
Harbour Road has several cafés, a bakery and two second-hand bookshops, and it is closed to traffic on Sundays.
The festival is organised by volunteers and a group of local businesses, and it has been running for eleven years.
quests.hint: Look for a because / so link where one thing leads to another.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence shows crowds causing sell-outs. The others only give facts about festivals, the street and the organisers.

quests.instruction: Which sentence links cause and effect correctly?
quests.prompt: The cinema raised its ticket prices, and fewer students now come on weeknights.
options: Ticket prices are higher, so cinemas are old and beautiful buildings.
The cinema raised its prices, and it has six screens and a café.
Since the cinema raised its prices, fewer students come on weeknights.
Students come on weeknights, so the cinema raised its ticket prices.
quests.hint: Check which event happened first and which one followed as a result.
quests.explanation: The price rise comes first and the drop in students follows. One option reverses the order, one links unrelated facts and one draws an illogical conclusion.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that show cause and effect.
quests.prompt: A writer is collecting examples for a community newsletter.
options: The bus stop is on the corner of Elm Road and Market Street, opposite the small row of shops.
When the school added a homework club, more students finished their assignments on time.
The homework club meets in Room 12 on Tuesdays and Thursdays, straight after the last lesson of the day.
Because the bus stop has no shelter, many passengers wait inside nearby shops when it rains.
quests.hint: Look for a sentence where one thing makes another thing happen.
quests.explanation: Each correct sentence shows that one event produced a result. The others simply say where or when something happens.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best explains what the evidence shows.
quests.prompt: Evidence: After the canteen added a salad bar, fruit sales rose from 30 to 75 portions a day.
options: Salad bars are popular in restaurants around the world, and many of them offer fruit as well.
Seventy-five is a bigger number than thirty portions, and the difference is easy to see.
The canteen sells fruit on every day of the school week, and it is placed near the tills.
This suggests students choose fruit more often when it is easy to see and reach.
quests.hint: An explanation says what the evidence means, not just repeats it.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence gives a reason for the rise in sales. The other choices restate numbers or add general facts.

quests.instruction: Choose the best explanation of the evidence.
quests.prompt: Evidence: Since the study centre added a silent floor, noise complaints fell from 21 to 7 per term.
options: Twenty-one complaints about noise were made in the earlier term, mostly on weekday afternoons.
This shows that separating quiet and social spaces reduces conflict between students.
Complaints are made through a form at the front desk, and a member of staff reads them each week.
The study centre has three floors, a small café and a row of computers near the entrance.
quests.hint: What does the drop in complaints tell us about the change?
quests.explanation: The correct sentence explains why the drop matters. The remaining options describe the complaints process or repeat details.

quests.instruction: Choose the explanation that best fits the personal evidence.
quests.prompt: Evidence: When I started planning meals on Sundays, my weekly food bill dropped from £85 to £62.
options: Sunday is a day when many people go to the supermarket.
Food shops charge different prices for very similar products.
£62 is smaller than £85 by a difference of £23.
Planning helped me buy only what I would use, which cut waste and cost.
quests.hint: Explain how the action led to the result.
quests.explanation: The right sentence explains how planning reduced spending. The alternatives repeat, generalise or calculate without explaining.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the explanation (it says what the evidence means)?
quests.prompt: 'Bike-share use rose by 30% in May. The weather was dry for three weeks. This suggests dry spells make people more willing to ride. The scheme has 40 stations.'
options: This suggests dry spells make people more willing to ride.
The weather was dry for three weeks.
Bike-share use rose by 30% in May.
The scheme has 40 stations.
quests.hint: The explanation begins to interpret the facts and explain why.
quests.explanation: The third sentence interprets the facts to say why use rose. The other choices give facts.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the evidence?
quests.prompt: A paragraph has four sentences: a claim, evidence, an explanation and a closing suggestion. Choose the evidence.
options: We should test a stand-up format for one month.
That is a large share of the week that could be used better.
Last quarter, our weekly meeting ran for 70 minutes on average.
Stand-up meetings would save our team a great deal of time.
quests.hint: Evidence is a measurable fact, not a claim, comment or suggestion.
quests.explanation: The 70-minute average is a measurable fact. The other sentences are a claim, an interpretation and a recommendation.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that explains, rather than repeats, the evidence.
quests.prompt: Evidence: Customers who received a text when their order was ready collected it within ten minutes.
options: The shop sends its texts between nine in the morning and six in the evening, and never at weekends.
Customers who are told when an order is ready do not need to keep checking, so they arrive at the right time.
Customers collected their orders within ten minutes of the text, whatever time of day it arrived.
Some customers received a text and some customers did not receive one, depending on how they had ordered.
quests.hint: An explanation gives the reason behind the result.
quests.explanation: The best sentence tells why the text helped. The alternatives restate the result or describe how the system works.

quests.instruction: Choose the comparison that works as evidence.
quests.prompt: Claim: Studying in short sessions works better than long ones.
options: Short study sessions are recommended in a number of well-known study guides written by experienced teachers.
Students who study in short sessions usually feel more positive about their work than students who study for hours.
Students who studied in 25-minute sessions recalled 70% of the material, compared with 50% for those who studied for two hours straight.
Studying for two hours straight is a very long time for most people, and many of them lose focus quickly.
quests.hint: A comparison places two results side by side using the same measure.
quests.explanation: The best sentence compares the same result for both methods. The alternatives give feelings, length or recommendations.

quests.instruction: Choose the fairest comparison.
quests.prompt: Claim: Cycling to work is quicker than driving in the city centre.
options: The same 5 km commute took 18 minutes by bike and 31 minutes by car at 8 a.m.
My bike trip on a Sunday took 15 minutes, and my car trip at Monday rush hour took 30.
Cars are larger than bicycles and generally cost far more to buy.
A 2 km bike ride took 10 minutes, while a 15 km drive took 25 minutes.
quests.hint: A fair comparison keeps distance and conditions the same.
quests.explanation: Only the first comparison uses the same distance and time of day. Others compare different distances or conditions, or do not compare speed.

quests.instruction: Which comparison best supports the claim?
quests.prompt: Claim: Our new website is easier to use.
options: The new website has a modern design with bright and cheerful colours.
Before the redesign, 35% of customers finished checkout; afterwards, 52% did.
Some customers said the old website was slow to load on their phones.
Before the redesign, the old website had around 120 pages in total.
quests.hint: Look for a before-and-after measure of ease of use.
quests.explanation: The checkout completion rates show an improvement. The other options describe appearance, size or a different problem.

quests.instruction: Choose the example that shows the practical value of the skill.
quests.prompt: Claim: Learning first aid is useful.
options: A first-aid kit contains plasters, bandages, scissors and gloves, and it should be checked every few months.
Many people say that first aid is an important skill to have, and most workplaces encourage staff to learn it.
First-aid courses usually last one or two days at a local centre and end with a short practical assessment.
A colleague who had taken a first-aid course stopped a cut from bleeding until the ambulance arrived.
quests.hint: A practical example shows the skill being used.
quests.explanation: The colleague's action shows first aid making a difference. The alternatives describe courses, opinions or kit contents.

quests.instruction: Choose the best practical example.
quests.prompt: Claim: Labelling food in a shared fridge reduces arguments.
options: After we added names and dates to containers, nobody accidentally ate a colleague's lunch.
Fridges in offices are usually cleaned by staff every Friday afternoon.
Labels can be bought in packs of one hundred from most stationers.
Some people bring their lunch from home every day of the week.
quests.hint: The example should show what changed after labelling.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence shows the effect of labels. The others mention fridges, labels or lunches without showing the result.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO practical examples.
quests.prompt: Claim: Learning to budget helps students avoid money stress.
options: Money is what people use to buy goods and services in shops.
A student who tracked spending found £30 a month going on snacks and cut it back.
By setting aside £20 each week, one student paid for her bus pass by autumn.
Budgeting is a topic in many school maths courses across the country.
quests.hint: Which sentences show a student actually using budgeting?
quests.explanation: Both correct answers show a student taking action and getting a result. The alternatives are general statements.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in order: claim, evidence, explanation, closing.
quests.prompt: Arrange these sentences about a weekly briefing.
options: Last quarter, seated briefings averaged 40 minutes, but our two standing trials lasted 15.
Our team should hold the Monday briefing standing up.
A shorter briefing leaves more of Monday for real work.
People are less likely to wander off topic when they are not settled in chairs.
quests.hint: The explanation comes after the evidence, since it tells us what the evidence means.
quests.explanation: The claim opens the paragraph, the comparison gives evidence, the explanation says why, and the last sentence links to the benefit.

quests.instruction: Order the sentences.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about food waste at school.
options: In one week, students threw away 18 kilograms of fruit peel and crusts.
Most of that waste could have become soil for the school garden instead.
Compost bins would turn wasted food into something useful.
Our school should place compost bins near the canteen.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that says what should happen.
quests.explanation: The claim leads, the weekly figure is the evidence, the third sentence explains what the evidence means, and the closing returns to the claim.

quests.instruction: Order the sentences.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about tracking spending.
options: Students should learn to track their spending early.
In a survey of 60 first-year students, 44 said they ran out of money before the end of term.
A simple spending diary would help them fix it sooner.
Without a record of where their money went, they could not spot the problem.
quests.hint: Ask which sentence would come first if you explained the point to a friend.
quests.explanation: The recommendation opens, the survey gives evidence, the explanation shows why the survey matters, and the closing suggests an action.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that connects the evidence to the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Walking meetings are better than desk meetings. Evidence: Staff at one firm take 15% more steps on days with walking meetings.
options: Walking is one of the oldest and simplest forms of exercise.
More movement can raise energy and attention, which makes discussions more productive.
Staff at the firm also drink more water on those particular days.
The firm has offices in two different cities and employs many staff.
quests.hint: The evidence shows steps. What is the link between steps and better meetings?
quests.explanation: The correct sentence explains why extra movement would improve meetings. The other choices add unrelated or additional facts.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best links the evidence to the claim?
quests.prompt: Claim: Cafés should offer free water refills. Evidence: In a survey of 100 customers, 64 said they buy bottled water only because they cannot get tap water.
options: Bottled water is sold in supermarkets, petrol stations and vending machines, often at high prices.
Sixty-four is more than half of the one hundred customers asked, so the result is a clear majority.
Customers often visit cafés with friends, family or work colleagues, and stay for around an hour.
With free refills, most of those customers would stop buying bottled water and plastic use would fall.
quests.hint: Show what would happen if the claim became reality.
quests.explanation: The right sentence connects the survey to the goal of reducing plastic. The remaining options repeat numbers or add background.

quests.instruction: Choose the explanation that makes the evidence support the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our club should add a beginner night. Evidence: Twelve people tried the club last term and none came back after the first session.
options: Some members have played the game for more than ten years.
The club meets on Wednesday evenings at the community hall.
Newcomers may feel out of place in sessions designed for experienced members.
Twelve people is a small number of people for any club to measure.
quests.hint: Why might newcomers leave after one session?
quests.explanation: This sentence gives a reason for the drop-off that a beginner night would fix. The alternatives weaken the evidence or add facts.

quests.instruction: Choose the best evidence.
quests.prompt: Claim: The new bus lane has reduced journey times on Route 5.
options: Timetable records from this year show the average trip on Route 5 shortened by six minutes.
A 2009 study from another country found that bus lanes can reduce delays.
A friend reported one unusually fast trip on the route on Thursday.
A newspaper article described the history of buses in the region.
quests.hint: Look for evidence that is current, local and about this route.
quests.explanation: Current records for this route directly test the claim. The alternatives are old, foreign, anecdotal or general.

quests.instruction: Choose the most useful evidence.
quests.prompt: Claim: Restaurants in our area are struggling with rising costs.
options: A blog post about one restaurant closing down last year.
A television show about the lives of famous chefs.
A survey of 40 restaurant owners in our area conducted last month.
A 2005 survey of restaurant owners in a different country.
quests.hint: Ask which evidence is recent and from the right place.
quests.explanation: A recent local survey matches the claim's time and place. The other sources are outdated, foreign, single cases or entertainment.

quests.instruction: Which evidence is LEAST useful for the claim?
quests.prompt: Claim: Students at our school need more sports facilities.
options: A student survey at our school on access to the gym.
The waiting list for the football pitch has 40 names on it.
Our school's sports hall is booked every lunchtime by different teams.
A national report about the popularity of professional sport.
quests.hint: Which piece of evidence says nothing about our school?
quests.explanation: A national report on professional sport doesn't show demand at our school. The alternatives show real pressure on the school's facilities.

quests.instruction: Choose the paragraph that has a claim, relevant evidence AND an explanation.
quests.prompt: Four students wrote about the length of the lunch break.
options: Employees should get a full hour for lunch. In a survey of 50 colleagues, those with thirty-minute breaks reported feeling tired by 3 p.m. The survey was completed in March and shared by email.

Employees should get a full hour for lunch. Our office has a canteen with sixty seats and a kitchen on each floor. A longer break gives people time to eat properly and rest, which helps them stay alert.
Employees should get a full hour for lunch. A longer break gives people time to eat properly and rest, which helps them stay alert. Most employers would agree that staying alert is important at work.

Employees should get a full hour for lunch. In a survey of 50 colleagues, those with thirty-minute breaks reported feeling tired by 3 p.m. A longer break gives people time to eat properly and rest, which helps them stay alert.
quests.hint: Check each paragraph for all three parts.
quests.explanation: This paragraph offers survey evidence and explains why it matters. The alternatives lack an explanation, lack evidence, or use evidence that does not relate to the claim.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest paragraph.
quests.prompt: Four paragraphs argue that the school should offer free after-class tutoring.
options: The school should offer free after-class tutoring. The science labs at the school were repainted last year. Free sessions would give students a fair chance to catch up.
The school should offer free after-class tutoring. Free sessions would give students a fair chance to catch up. Fairness is something that all schools should care about in the end.

The school should offer free after-class tutoring. Last term, 26 of the 40 students who failed the science test said they could not afford a tutor. Free sessions would give them a fair chance to catch up.

The school should offer free after-class tutoring. Last term, 26 of the 40 students who failed the science test said they could not afford a tutor. The school was founded in 1962 and has three science labs.
quests.hint: The best paragraph links evidence to the claim in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The correct paragraph shows a need and then explains how tutoring would meet it. The other choices end with irrelevant details, no evidence, or unrelated evidence.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best fills the gap.
quests.prompt: 'Cafés should add a quiet hour each morning. In one café, 18 of 25 regular customers said they left because of loud music. ____ A quiet hour would keep those customers coming back.'
options: Loud music is played in many cafés, shops and gyms every day.
Customers who want to read or work need calm surroundings to stay for long.
A quiet hour could begin at eight and end at nine in the morning.
Eighteen of the twenty-five customers asked were regular visitors.
quests.hint: The missing sentence should explain how the evidence supports the claim.
quests.explanation: The right sentence explains why loud music drives away certain customers, connecting the survey to the quiet hour. The remaining options repeat, describe or give unrelated details.

quests.instruction: Choose the best explanation of the evidence.
quests.prompt: Evidence: Since paying by phone began, the average queue at the town's parking machines dropped from six minutes to two.
options: Two minutes is a shorter length of time than six minutes.
Parking machines can be found in most town centres and car parks.
Paying by phone requires a mobile signal and a bank card.
Drivers no longer wait behind people searching for coins, so the line moves faster.
quests.hint: Which sentence tells why the queue got shorter?
quests.explanation: The best sentence explains the mechanism behind the result. The alternatives repeat, describe or list a possible drawback.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO problems with this evidence.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our team's new schedule is a success. Evidence: Last Tuesday, one manager said she liked it.
options: It reflects the view of only one person.
It records an opinion, not a measured result.
It gives the name of a day instead of a date.
It was given on a Tuesday, not on a Monday.
quests.hint: Think about how many people it covers and what kind of information it gives.
quests.explanation: One person's opinion cannot show that a schedule is successful. The day of the week is unimportant, and the person's job title is a smaller issue than the missing measurements.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in order: claim, evidence, explanation, closing.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about a monthly game evening.
options: A monthly board game night would strengthen our team.
One evening a month is a small step toward a friendlier office.
Playing together gives people a relaxed reason to talk about more than work.
After the trial evening, 14 of 20 attendees said they knew a colleague better than before.
quests.hint: The claim comes first and the closing leaves the reader with the benefit.
quests.explanation: The claim leads, the survey result is the evidence, the explanation shows how a game night helps, and the closing sums up.
